cut: v1 stills (6 Nov, en only): the ART test the owner asked for after Cut First did well (6 Nov: 'maybe it's the art, maybe the topic, maybe both'). Same 3D toy-world cars look as Cut First, a different, non-Finnish topic: AI servers under US export controls reaching China anyway, per prosecutors. Five beats: the export gate says no; a ship takes the long way round a toy sea (Taiwan, Southeast Asia); the labelled crates go through a repack line and come out plain; a hair dryer moves a serial sticker from a real server onto a dummy; the inspectors are shown a row of dummies while the ship heads for China. For the owner's approval, not for posting.
argument: Prosecutors say about $2.5B of AI servers that need a licence for China were routed there via Taiwan and Southeast Asia, repacked in unmarked boxes, with dummies shown to inspectors.
syntax: '/' breaks a line, [word] is the pop word

text.en: These AI servers / can't go to China / without a [licence].

captions.source: US export controls require a licence to export advanced AI chips, and servers built with them, to China. Under the rules in force in 2024-25 (the period of the alleged scheme) licences were presumptively denied; since 15 Jan 2026 BIS reviews H200-class licences case by case (Federal Register 2026-00789; Mayer Brown, Jan 2026). 'Without a licence' is true under both regimes.

Indictment unsealed in the Southern District of New York, 19 Mar 2026: three people charged with conspiring to divert about $2.5B of servers with Nvidia AI chips to China, sales in 2024-25 (Bloomberg Government, The Register 20 Mar, Al Jazeera 20 Mar, eWeek, Tom's Hardware). Attributed to prosecutors; nobody convicted at trial. From search summaries; the indictment itself was not opened.

Prosecutors say servers went from the US to facilities in Taiwan, then to a Southeast Asian company that repackaged them in unmarked boxes for China (eWeek; itnews; The Register; Fox News 'dummy servers'). From search summaries.

Prosecutors cite surveillance footage of a hair dryer used to move labels and serial-number stickers from real servers onto dummy servers (Tom's Hardware; The Stack 'the SVP, the hairdryer and the $2.5 billion'; The Next Web 'The dummy server and the chip war'). Attributed; from search summaries.

Prosecutors say thousands of non-working dummy servers were staged to deceive the manufacturer's compliance team, ahead of a US Commerce Department inspection, and during a visit by a US export control officer (Fox News; itnews; The Next Web; The Stack). 'Were shown' (not 'checked') because that is what is alleged. Attributed; from search summaries.

post.en: US prosecutors say three people linked to Super Micro sent ~$2.5B of servers with Nvidia AI chips to China via Taiwan and Southeast Asia, in unmarked boxes, and showed inspectors dummies. One has pleaded guilty; the company isn't charged. Who checks the boxes?
